channel.title: The Night Desk
channel.description: News for the Graveyard Crew — true crime, breaking news, and the stories that keep you up at night.

item.title: Guilty on all 7 counts in Milwaukee triple homicide — Zollicoffer verdict
item.description: A Milwaukee County jury convicted Thomas Zollicoffer, 37, on Thursday of three counts of first-degree intentional homicide and four counts of possession of a firearm by a felon in the Aug. 8 killings of three people in two shootings. Sentencing is set for Nov. 20.

item.title: PS5 Storage, Round Two: Making Room for the Holiday Game Wave
item.description: Round two on PS5 storage: the holiday game wave is bigger than launch day — the three storage tiers, the library triage, and the two install details that decide whether the gift games fit on Christmas night.

item.title: Water Softener Salt: The Upkeep Schedule Nobody Tells You
item.description: Choosing salt was the easy part. The upkeep rhythm — the two-minute monthly check, bridging, stocking for guest season, and the once-a-year clean-out — is what keeps a softener working in year three.

item.title: Night-Shift Commute, Holiday Edition: Equipping the Driver, Not Just the Car
item.description: The winter car kit equips the car; this one equips the driver — alertness that actually works, the in-cab kit, and surviving the Christmas schedule flip on night shift.

item.title: The Two-Week Runway: Christmas Household Prep Without the December Meltdown
item.description: Christmas household prep sequenced over fourteen days: guest capacity, kitchen capacity, power capacity, and the small stuff — batteries, tape, defrost math — that ambushes people.

item.title: In custody — suspect surrenders in fatal Mundy Township McDonald's shooting
item.description: Willie James Kennebrew Jr., 18, surrendered to Genesee County Sheriff's deputies on Tuesday, Nov. 17, five days after the fatal shooting inside the McDonald's at 6015 Hill 23 Dr. in Mundy Township. He is charged with first-degree premeditated murder in the death of Jalen Sims Daniels, 18, a McDonald's employee.

item.title: Manhunt in Genesee County — suspect sought in fatal Mundy Township McDonald's shooting
item.description: Metro Police Authority investigators are searching for Willie James Kennebrew Jr., 18, identified as a suspect in the Nov. 12 fatal shooting inside the McDonald's at 6015 Hill 23 Dr. in Mundy Township. Police say he is armed and dangerous and may have left Mid-Michigan.

item.title: The Night-Shift Drive Home: A Commute Kit for the Hardest Miles of the Day
item.description: The drive home is the most dangerous part of a night shift. The alertness layer, the trunk breakdown kit, and rule zero: a nap beats every gadget on the list.

item.title: Toddler Waterpark Days: The Swim Gear That Actually Earns Its Bag Space
item.description: An approved, weight-matched vest, swim diapers times three, and sun gear that stays on: the short list of toddler swim gear that earns its space in the bag.

item.title: Water Softener Salt, Explained: Types, How Much Your Tank Takes, and Storing It
item.description: Pellets, solar, rock, or potassium chloride — what the bags actually are, how much a typical brine tank takes, and the two-minute monthly check that keeps a softener working.

item.title: A First 3D Printer, Without the Buyer's Remorse: What the Specs Actually Mean
item.description: Auto leveling, a PEI flex plate, direct drive: how to read a first-printer listing, what the filament choices mean, and the small kit that prevents big headaches.

item.title: PS5 Headsets for Late-Night Sessions: Hear Everything, Wake Nobody
item.description: Game sound in, house sound out: the four specs that matter for a PS5 headset when kids are asleep in the next room, and the settings that matter as much as the hardware.

item.title: Back to PlayStation After Years Away: The PS5 Accessories Worth Buying First
item.description: Coming back to PlayStation after years away? The honest accessory order — a second controller, a charging dock, and a headset first — and what to skip for now.

item.title: A Play Space That Survives a Toddler: The Short, Honest Setup List
item.description: The short, honest setup list for a toddler play space: furniture anchors and outlet covers first, then a thick foam mat and storage a small person can actually use.

item.title: Night-Shift Sleep: Small Gear That Makes Daytime Sleep Actually Work
item.description: Daytime sleep is an environment problem, and environment problems have gear answers: blackout curtains, a sleep mask, white noise, and earplugs — in the order to buy them.

item.title: The Household Emergency Binder: What Actually Belongs in One (and What Doesn't)
item.description: What actually belongs in a household emergency binder, what doesn't, and how to keep it safe — plus the ready-made version from our own storefront.

item.title: PS5 Storage, Solved: How to Choose an External Drive for a Growing Game Library
item.description: Two different PS5 storage problems, two different answers: an external USB drive for the archive, an internal NVMe SSD for playable space — how to choose, in plain terms.

item.title: Two killed in Mount Pleasant apartment shooting — police believe one of the deceased was the shooter
item.description: Michigan State Police say a 21-year-old man from Jackson and an 18-year-old woman from Ludington died in the Nov. 14 Copper Beech shooting in Mount Pleasant. An 18-year-old Mount Pleasant man was treated and released. Investigators believe one of the deceased was the shooter.

item.title: Dazman Drake found guilty of first-degree murder in Port Huron killing of Vincent Buckles
item.description: A St. Clair County jury found Dazman Drake, 24, guilty of first-degree murder on Friday, Nov. 13, for the Jan. 28, 2025 shooting death of Vincent Buckles in his Port Huron home. Drake was also convicted of home invasion and other charges; sentencing is Dec. 14, and he faces up to life in prison.

item.title: Rex Ryan surrenders in Nashville, charged in Broadway hit-and-run that injured two pedestrians
item.description: Former NFL head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan surrendered to Metro Nashville Police on Nov. 11 and was booked on misdemeanor charges tied to a Nov. 5 hit-and-run on Broadway, where police say a truck ran over two pedestrians' feet and one leg, the driver argued with the victims, and then drove away.
